# Provider fixtures

Responses the injected HTTP transport replays in tests. The `openai/` files are hand-written from OpenAI's documented response shapes, not captured from live calls; replace them with real captures (Credentials removed) during the live smoke test (#11).

The OpenAI error responses (`invalid-api-key`, `insufficient-quota`, `billing-hard-limit-reached`, `rate-limit-exceeded`, `moderation-blocked`, `content-policy-violation`, `server-error`) follow OpenAI's documented `{ "error": { "message", "type", "param", "code" } }` shape; the tests pair each with the HTTP status OpenAI sends it with. `edits.json` answers `/images/edits`, which responds in the same shape as `/images/generations`.

The `gemini/` files are likewise hand-written, from Google's Interactions API docs (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation, https://ai.google.dev/api/interactions-api and https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-errors), not captured from live calls; replace them during the live smoke test (#11). `interaction.json` is a completed Interaction whose `thought` step carries an interim image (which litevision must ignore) before the `model_output` step with the final image. `interaction-blocked.json` is a safety block delivered as HTTP 200 (`status: "failed"`, `errors[].code: "image_safety"`); `interaction-text-only.json` is a completed Interaction with text and no image. The HTTP errors use the Interactions `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }` shape, except `api-key-invalid.json`, which uses Google's older `{ "error": { "code", "message", "status", "details" } }` shape with reason `API_KEY_INVALID`, as `/models` answers. `models.json` and `models-page-2.json` are two pages of `GET /models`, linked by `nextPageToken`.

The `apimart/` files are hand-written from APIMart's official docs (https://docs.apimart.ai/en), also not live captures; #11 replaces them. Sources:

- `submitted.json`, and the `{ "error": { "code", "message", "type" } }` errors `invalid-api-key` (401), `insufficient-balance` (402) and `rate-limit` (429): the response examples on the GPT-Image-2 page (`api-reference/images/gpt-image-2/generation`).
- `task-*.json`: Get Task Status (`api-reference/tasks/status`). `task-completed.json` follows its documented example, where `result.images[].url` is an array; `pending`, `processing`, `failed` and `cancelled` keep that shape with the fields the page lists for each status. The moderation message in `task-failed-moderation.json` is made up; the page documents only the `error` object's fields.
- `models.json`: Models List Metadata (`api-reference/texts/models/list`) with `expand=category`.
- `schema-gpt-image-2.json`: that page says `GET /v1/models/{model}/schema` answers in the same shape as one list item with `expand=parameters`. Its `input_schema` is filled in from the GPT-Image-2 page's request fields.

The `venice/` files are hand-written from Venice's API reference and OpenAPI spec (https://docs.venice.ai, `https://api.venice.ai/doc/api/swagger.yaml`), not captured from live calls; replace them during #11 too. `models-image.json` and `models-inpaint.json` answer `GET /models?type=image` and `?type=inpaint`, with one model of each sizing style: `widthHeightDivisor` above 1 (`venice-sd35`, sized in pixels), `aspectRatios` only (`qwen-image-2`), and `aspectRatios` plus `resolutions` (`nano-banana-pro`); the edit models carry `maxInputImages` or `combineImages: false`. `generate*.json` answer `/image/generate`, including a partial result with `content_policy_violation_count`. The error files follow Venice's documented `{ "error", "code" }` shape; the tests pair each with its HTTP status. `/image/edit` and `/image/multi-edit` answer with raw image bytes, so the tests reply with a PNG directly.
